candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Epistola ad Marcellinum §20
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Marcellinum de Interpretatione Psalmorum (Letter to Marcellinus on the Interpretation of the Psalms), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 27 (1857). The Letter is Athanasius's principal pastoral-spiritual work — a personal letter to Marcellinus (recovering from illness) explaining how to use each Psalm as prayer for specific spiritual circumstances. Hermeneutic anchor for the Tewahedo Office (Säʿatat) Psalter-recitation tradition.
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Epistola ad Marcellinum §20 (c. 350 AD)

'He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty' (LXX 90:1 — ho katoikōn en boētheia tou Hypsistou en skepē tou theou tou ouranou aulisthēsetai) — Athanasius marks Ps 91 (LXX 90) as the DIVINE-PROTECTION PARADIGM in the Letter to Marcellinus: prescribed for the soul-seeking-refuge-from-physical-and-spiritual-dangers. The shadow-of-the-Most-High (skepē tou Hypsistou) is read Christ-ologically — the Word-incarnate is the divine-shadow-cast-on-earth, the Annunciation-overshadowing (Lk 1:35 episkiasei soi) now-extended to every believer. The Tewahedo travel-blessing tradition cites Ps 91 as the Mäzmurä Dawit (David's Psalter) protective-prayer.
